title: holdout-verdict contract data
description: Reference schema (FAFF-34). The SHAPE of the code-blind holdout verdict the `evaluator` slot's producer (default faffter-noon-evaluate) emits after exercising a built feature against its spec in a provisioned env. Shape is normative here; the verdict SEMANTICS (the aggregate derivation, the prose->needs-human rule) live in the gateway / ADR-0032. Fail-loud on a non-object input (no safe coerce target — faff's own producer emits it). `aggregate`, each criterion's `class`, and each `verdict` are plain strings here: their enums ({meets-spec,gaps,fails,needs-human} / {scenario,assertion,prose} / {met,unmet,needs-human}) are enforced in the compute fn via violations (the env-handle/architecture-proposal precedent), so an echoed bad value is exit 1, never a spurious schemaCheck fail-loud (exit 2). The compute fn also enforces the cross-field rules that make exit 0: code_blind MUST be true; a prose criterion MUST be needs-human; a met/unmet criterion MUST carry evidence; and the aggregate MUST match the derivation from the criteria — fail-safe coercion is toward needs-human, never meets-spec. FAFF-384 adds the OPTIONAL, additive `spawner_attested` + `attestation` fields: when a run's lane-boundary intent promised an evaluator cage, the spawner (never the judged party) sets code_blind from what it provably withheld, and the compute fn's caller-resolved `--require-spawner-attested` ratchet rejects a verdict lacking spawner_attested:true. Absent these fields, a legacy (uncaged) verdict validates byte-for-byte as before. FAFF-1291 adds the OPTIONAL `delegated` array: the criteria the holdout did not judge, each with the verifier that covers it (a prose DONE item goes to the AC checklist, an integration-tier criterion to the review and merge test floor). The `aggregate` is derived over `criteria` only, so `meets-spec` means every judged criterion was met, not that the whole DoD was met; delegated prose DONE items rest on the builder-written AC checklist and the review leg (FAFF-1339 will check each delegated `ac_id` has a passed checklist row). The compute fn enforces the delegation rules (a prose criterion with a done:N id is never judged; the tier and verifier pair; no id in both lists).
